title: Estimators: ML, robust ML, ordinal data and FIML
summary: Maximum likelihood assumes multivariate normality; robust ML keeps its estimates but corrects standard errors and the test, ordinal items may need ordinal estimators, and FIML uses all available data under MAR.

body.text: [[maximum-likelihood]] (ML) is the default CB-SEM estimator. Its estimates are consistent under fairly general conditions, but its standard errors and χ² test assume multivariate normality. [[mlr]] keeps the ML estimates and replaces the standard errors with robust (sandwich) ones and the test with a scaled statistic (Yuan & Bentler 2000). In SEM Studio, ML and MLR give identical point estimates; only SEs, p values and the scaled fit indices differ.

Rating items are ordinal. With five or more roughly symmetric categories, ML or MLR on the raw items usually performs acceptably; with fewer categories or strong skew, diagonally weighted least squares on polychoric correlations ([[wlsmv]]) is preferable (Flora & Curran 2004; Rhemtulla et al. 2012). SEM Studio's browser engine offers ML and MLR; WLSMV and MLM are not available in it.

Missing data: [[listwise-deletion]] drops every case with any missing value; it is unbiased only if data are missing completely at random and wastes information. [[fiml]] uses every observed value and is unbiased under missing at random (Enders & Bandalos 2001; Schafer & Graham 2002). In the missing-mcar data listwise deletion keeps 258 of 500 cases; FIML uses all 500. SEM Studio supports FIML for CB-SEM with a mean structure; it is not defined for PLS-SEM.
State the [[missing-data-mechanism]] you assume (MCAR, MAR) and why; FIML does not fix data that are missing not at random.

mistake.title: Thinking MLR changes the estimates
mistake.text: MLR is not a different model: loadings and paths are the same as ML. If a result changes "with MLR", only its standard error or p value changed.

tryIt.task: Run this two-factor CFA with listwise deletion, then set missing-data handling to FIML (with a mean structure) and run again. Compare the number of cases used and the factor correlation.

checks.question: You re-run a CB model with MLR instead of ML. What changes?

options.text: Standard errors, p values and the (scaled) test statistic; the estimates stay the same.

options.feedback: MLR uses the ML estimates; only the inference around them changes.
The standard errors and the test statistic are corrected for non-normality.

checks.question: About 8% of cells are missing at random across eight items. Which approach does the literature favour for CB-SEM?

options.feedback: Correct. It uses all available information and is unbiased under MAR.
Here it would discard about half of the cases, losing power, and it requires the stricter MCAR assumption.

options.text: Replacing missing values by the item mean
options.feedback: Mean substitution shrinks variances and correlations and biases estimates.

checks.explanation: Prefer FIML (or multiple imputation) under MAR.
